title: Diagnosis of Package 79 Force Discontinuity and KKT Active-Set Membership Audit
finding: Diagnosed dominant root cause of Package 79 reaction-force discrepancy (+258% increase to 11.71 N in Step 2, +58.68% at terminal Step 3): unweighted element-to-node damage averaging across the crack wake broadened the profile and diluted damage (d = 0.9928 vs donor Gauss-point d = 0.9971), increasing the residual wake stiffness integral int(g(d)*dx) by 1.981x (1.287e-4 mm vs donor 6.499e-5 mm) and transmitting an unphysical ~8.44 N elastic wake force. In Step 3, unconstrained crack-tip nodes attempted to shed this excess energy through severe localized softening (d jumping from 0.785 to 0.924), causing Newton iteration cutback down to dt < 1e-12 at increment 16. Active-set audit verified that all 9 healing nodes were in the inactive set (min delta_d = -0.00040) and must be activated, while 13 negative multiplier nodes (min lambda = -1.10e-6) were active and must be released, updating partitions to |A_{k+1}| = 1,752 and |I_{k+1}| = 661. In accordance with policy, new execution is withheld until wake-damage mapping is corrected. Method C Gate C1-1 criteria remain strictly FAILED.
next_operation: Prepare Package 80 candidate deck with wake-damage mapping correction to restore donor ligament stiffness compliance and eliminate artificial elastic prestress
